subject.declared_domain: NFRA_PROMOTE R4 -- the in-VPC PROMOTE CSE producer, the governed 5th producer's FEDOBS-feed wiring. A recognizer MATERIALIZED/DEMOTED transition is itself an observation (PROMOTE invariant #5), emitted as a schema-validated CSE into globgrph.cse alongside git/graph_head/agent/deploy. Declared REUSE-NOT-REBUILD: the CSE is built by comp_promote_materializer._build_promote_cse so every emission is IDENTICAL to the materializer's own; this module adds only the live promotion state, an honest commission-vintage timestamp, and the JSONL projection for the derive-role ingest.

methodology.how: promote_cses (:99-123) reads the promotion manifest through the materializer's own helpers, iterates the recognizers, keeps only entries passing mat._loadable (state==MATERIALIZED with a non-null commission), and for each calls mat._build_promote_cse to construct the CSE -- the reuse contract, with validate_or_raise inside the builder. _stamp (:66-70) then overwrites the timestamp with the commission's own vintage so the store partitions by the real promotion date. An already_emitted set, when supplied, skips ids already in the store. dry_run (:142-160) is the DEFAULT with no arguments and writes nothing; emit (:162-183) validates fail-closed, writes the JSONL, and only then advances the emitted-marker.

cadence.declared_rhythm: EVENT-DRIVEN BY EXPLICIT CONTRACT, and this is the one producer on the face for which being unscheduled is the DESIGN rather than a gap. The standing-contract comment (:73-75, 'Q4 STANDING CONTRACT (CTO GO 2026-07-08)') states it emits on a promotion, not a clock, and that its 'incremental' is therefore an idempotent DEDUP: a re-run emits only promotions not already emitted, never a duplicate row in the append-only log. The emitted-event-id marker is also declared to be the S3 object a downstream leg watches.
cadence.actual_trigger: A HUMAN RUNNING THE CLI, then a separate in-VPC cse_store --ingest. Nothing schedules either, which the contract permits. What the contract does NOT permit is the dedup being inert -- and it is: the marker object the whole idempotency scheme reads and writes DOES NOT EXIST. MEASURED: head-object on warehouse/cse_producer_markers/promote.json returns 404, and the entire cse_producer_markers/ prefix holds ZERO keys, against a positive control (warehouse/_branch_head.main.json, 1508 B) proving the instrument reads. So _read_emitted returns an empty set on every invocation, and every --emit re-emits every current promotion as though for the first time.
cadence.live_instance_age: 53 DAYS. One row, event_date 2026-07-08, and the module's own docstring is dated 2026-07-08 -- so like the deploy producer this emitted once, on the day it was written. Unlike the deploy producer, that is not by itself a defect: an event-driven producer with no promotion to report is correctly silent. What makes it a finding is that the silence and the inert marker are indistinguishable -- a run today would re-emit the 2026-07-08 promotion, not nothing.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: THE AST CENSUS FINDS TWO HANDLERS AND ONLY ONE IS A DATA-PATH SWALLOW -- I am naming both because reporting the count alone would misattribute the second. :269 in main is `except Exception: pass` around sys.stdout/sys.stderr .reconfigure(errors='replace'), i.e. console-encoding setup; it cannot affect a CSE and I do not count it against the module. :85 in _read_emitted is the real one: `except Exception: return set()` around a boto3 get_object, so ANY failure -- absent object, denied access, throttle, expired credentials, network -- returns 'nothing has ever been emitted'. Everything else propagates: _write_emitted has no handler, promote_cses has none, and the builder validates or raises inside.
silent_degrade_paths: THE IDEMPOTENCY LEDGER FAILS OPEN, AND ITS OBJECT DOES NOT EXIST. _read_emitted (:80-86) cannot distinguish a genuine first run from a credentials or permissions failure -- its own comment fuses them -- and both yield an empty set, which means re-emit everything. MEASURED: the marker is absent (404; the whole prefix is empty; positive control reads). So today the dedup is not merely fragile, it is INERT: every --emit re-emits every MATERIALIZED promotion. Because cse_store.append_cses does NOT deduplicate by event_id (cse_store.py:357-393, read in full), a second ingest appends DUPLICATE rows into an append-only log. The failure is silent in both directions: nothing prints when the marker read fails, and the run's own output looks identical to a correct first emission

verdict.why: This module is the most carefully REASONED on the face and several of its choices deserve to be recorded as strengths rather than absorbed. Its default with no arguments is a DRY RUN that writes nothing -- emitting requires an explicit --emit, which is the right way round and the opposite of the deploy producer's default-to-write. It reuses the materializer's own builder rather than reimplementing the CSE, and the live row's actor of comp_promote_materializer exercises that claim. It refuses to reconstruct demotes from a runtime trail that carries self-test and exercise records, and says why. And it carries a consumer note, repeated into its own output, warning FEDOBS not to discount a promote CSE for its LOW confidence band because that 0.2 is the subject's TYPE-confidence and not the promotion's certainty -- a genuinely unusual piece of care about how a downstream reader will misread a number. Being unscheduled is its DECLARED contract, so unlike the deploy producer I do not count that against it. QUALIFIED on three measured points. FIRST: the idempotency ledger fails open AND its object does not exist, so the dedup is inert today -- every --emit re-emits every promotion, and since append_cses does not deduplicate, a second ingest writes duplicate rows into an append-only log. The code's own comment fuses 'absent' and 'no-access' into one value. SECOND: the timestamp repair falls back to the empty string it was written to prevent, partition_key propagates that as an empty event_date without error, and the only check for it lives inside _self_test and is unreachable from the write path -- a guard in the one place it cannot fire. THIRD: four private cross-module names carry the reuse, with no signature on either side recording the coupling. I record one error of my own that reached a committed artifact: on card 2 I read a manufactured zero as a finding, and the correction is at b3b1705d26.
